item.title: Pope Returns to Peru, Where Evangelicals Challenge Catholic Dominance
item.description: Pope Leo spent nearly two decades in Peru, rising to bishop and becoming a citizen. But many Peruvians have turned away from Catholicism, seeking a more expressive and direct connection to God.
item.dc:creator: Julie Turkewitz and Marco Garro
item.media:credit: Marco Garro for The New York Times
item.media:description: Members of Agua Viva, a Pentecostal megachurch in Lima, Peru, attending a prayer concert.

item.title: Canadian Authorities Kill 4 Bears Involved in Deadly Attack on Hikers
item.description: Wildlife authorities said evidence, including animal DNA, conclusively linked a sow and her three cubs to the deaths of two women along a hiking trail in British Columbia.
item.dc:creator: Qasim Nauman
item.media:description: Selah Reed, left, and her mother, Jennifer Balcarras, were killed by grizzly bears in British Columbia earlier this month.

item.title: Passenger Arrested in Connection to Possible Homicide on Cruise Ship
item.description: The F.B.I. is investigating the death of a female passenger on the Caribbean-bound MSC Seascape, which departed from Galveston on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Ceylan Yeğinsu
item.media:credit: Kirk Sides/Houston Chronicle, via Getty Images
item.media:description: The MSC Seascape returned to port in Galveston, Texas, after the possible homicide of a passenger on the ship.

item.title: U.S. Received $12 Billion From Venezuela’s Oil, Report Shows
item.description: The workings of a U.S.-controlled bank account shed light on how Washington manages Venezuelan revenue after capturing the country’s president.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager and Anatoly Kurmanaev
item.media:description: An oil pump in Cabimas, Venezuela, in August. U.S. forces toppled the country’s president in January.

item.title: The Man Who Helped the C.I.A. Secretly Operate in Mexico
item.description: President Claudia Sheinbaum drew a firm line barring U.S. forces from operating on Mexican soil. But in a northern border state, one local partner quietly helped the agency build a foothold.
item.dc:creator: Steve Fisher and Jack Nicas
item.media:description: Mexican soldiers on patrol in Ciudad Juárez in Chihuahua State, Mexico, in August.

item.title: In Argentina, Pope Leo Walks in the Giant Shadow of Francis
item.description: Francis never returned to his home country after becoming pope, but the new pontiff will still be confronted with the overwhelming presence of his predecessor.
item.dc:creator: Emma Bubola and Sarah Pabst

item.title: Exxon Strikes Preliminary Deal to Return to Venezuela
item.description: The agreement brings the biggest U.S. oil company a step closer to pumping oil again in Venezuela, nearly two decades after it left the country.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Exxon Mobil already has major operations in Guyana, which shares a contested border with Venezuela.

item.title: Isabel Letelier, a Chilean Voice for Human Rights, Has Died

item.title: Megyn Kelly, Elon Musk and Others Defend Russell Brand After Rape Conviction

item.title: A Country’s President Led to a Bank’s Stunning Rise, and Its Fall
item.description: Prosecutors accused President Santiago Peña of Paraguay of funneling nearly a billion dollars of government funds to the Ueno bank as its executives made reckless insider loans.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Ellick and Laurence Blair
item.media:description: Protesters gathered outside the home of Santiago Peña, the president of Paraguay, in Asunción, the country’s capital, on Friday.

item.title: Targeted by U.S., Armed Group Strikes Back in Colombia
item.description: American forces are helping Colombia and Venezuela hunt the ELN. This weekend, the group attacked a Colombian military base with drones, officials said.

item.title: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Found in Smugglers’ Socks at Peru Airport
item.description: The National Forest and Wildlife Service of Peru said three people had tried to smuggle the tarantulas, which included a threatened species, into Germany.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Holpuch
item.media:credit: Peruvian National Forest and Wildlife Service, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: The spiders were seized at Jorge Chavéz International Airport in Lima, Peru, after receiving a tip, the authorities said.

item.title: In Argentina, Pope Leo Tells President Milei Economy Must Serve the Needy
item.description: The pontiff’s trip comes amid tensions between the country’s libertarian leader and its Catholic Church, which is deeply committed to social justice.

item.media:description: Catholic clergy members gathered for prayer last month after a march for social rights and justice in La Matanza, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina.

item.title: Giant Roadside Attractions Face Mounting Costs and an Uncertain Future

item.dc:creator: Karla Adam
item.media:description: At 86 feet tall, Tyra the Tyrannosaurus of Drumheller, Alberta, is about four times the size of a real T. rex.

item.title: Father Calls Daughter, the Co-Pilot Killed in Florida Crash, ‘a Hero’
item.description: Allan Filgueiras said during a news conference that his daughter, Nathalia, 20, fought to the final seconds as a private jet carrying nine people crashed near Palm Beach, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner

item.title: Inside the Nightclub Sheltering Haitians From Violent Gangs

item.title: King Charles Was Umbrella-Less but in His Element on Caribbean Tour

item.title: Prosecutors Charge Paraguay’s Former President With Corruption

item.description: A top adviser to President Javier Milei of Argentina met Flávio Bolsonaro, the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate, at an Argentine airport, three people involved in the operation said.

item.title: Canadian Officials Search for Bears After Mother and Daughter Are Killed on Hike
item.description: Wildlife officers were working to trap grizzly bears along a trail after the remains of the two hikers were found near a remote community in British Columbia this week.
item.dc:creator: Karla Adam
item.media:credit: Pat Kane for The New York Times
item.media:description: Officials are looking for links between the deaths this week and another grizzly bear attack in the same part of western Canada last year that injured four people.
